summary: Willamette NF lookout cab (dated 1930 by some sources, 1932 by a newspaper plan), L-4 cab and AWS cabin in 1942, gone by 1960 or burned in 1968.

facts.design: 8x8 foot cab; from 1942 an L-4 cab with an Air Warning Service cabin
facts.status_note: firetower.org and firelookout.com say gone by 1960; the Oregon lookout history site says it was disposed of by burning in 1968

events.note: 8x8 foot cab, per firetower.org and firelookout.com. A 1932 newspaper item (below) describes new lookout houses being packed in, so the first build date is uncertain
Eugene Guard items of August and September 1932 name Pack Saddle mountain for new lookout houses, with materials to be packed 12 to 15 miles in by horse
William G. Fowler left to serve as lookout fireman there (Eugene Register-Guard item)

Bend Bulletin item of July 31, 1939 on a fire at Mud Lake says the blaze was at the lake's south shore, by a Packsaddle mountain lookout station. The item does not say that station is the Willamette forest lookout; the link rests on the name
Eugene Guard item: Felix Sparks had just completed a lookout station at Pack Saddle mountain
8x8 cab replaced with an L-4 cab; an Air Warning Service cabin was added
Gone by 1960 per firetower.org and firelookout.com
Oregon lookout history site: the lookout was disposed of by burning

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org and firelookout.com date the 8x8 cab to 1930. A 1932 Eugene Guard item describes new lookout houses being planned and packed in for Pack Saddle mountain that year. The sources do not settle whether 1930 or the 1932 work was the first build. The story gives both.
firetower.org and firelookout.com say the lookout was gone by 1960. The Oregon lookout history site says it was disposed of by burning in 1968. The story gives both dates.

notes_for_editor: The build year (1930 on two sites, 1932 newspaper plan) and the end (gone by 1960 vs burned in 1968) disagree; the story gives both. No source describes what remains today or whether the site is open. Two search snippets (AllTrails 'Mcbee Trail to Packsaddle Mountain' route and PeakVisor, 1,873 m, which matches the record's 1,872.7 m) suggest a summit trail exists, but I could not read those pages (AllTrails returned 403), so they are not used. The brief's first source_pages URL (packsaddle-mountain-lane-county) returns 404; the registered URL is packsaddle-mountain-lookout-site-lane-county. Excluded namesake: Packsaddle Mountain in Idaho (Kaniksu NF), which has its own lookout history.
